entry.title: Data Reporting Requirements for Certain Event Contracts (CFTC Final Rule)
entry.summary: Data Reporting Requirements for Certain Event Contracts Federal Register · Nov 30, 2026 · Rule · Effective Jan 29, 2027The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is finalizing revisions to its regulations setting out an alternate data reporting framework for certain fully collateralized event contracts. Under the revisions, covered reporting markets, futures commission merchants, clearing members and foreign brokers report these contracts under parts 15 through 18 rather than certain sections of parts 38, 39, 43 and 45. The rule takes effect January 29, 2027. The archived text and attachments run to about 408,445 characters; the summary is based only on the first 12,000. entry.title: IRS sets higher interest rates for Q1 2027
entry.summary: Interest rates increase for the first quarter of 2027 IRS · Nov 24, 2026 · GuidanceThe IRS announced that for the calendar quarter beginning January 1, 2027, the interest rate on individual overpayments and underpayments will be 8% per year, compounded daily, and 7% for corporate overpayments. The rate on corporate overpayments above $10,000 is 5.5%, and the rate for large corporate underpayments is 10%. The rates are based on the federal short-term rate determined in October 2026. entry.title: CFTC issues final rule on data reporting for certain event contracts
entry.summary: CFTC Publishes Final Rule Concerning Data Reporting Requirements for Certain Event Contracts CFTC · Nov 23, 2026 · RuleThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced approval of a final rule amending Parts 15, 16, and 17 of its regulations. It sets out an alternate framework for reporting data on certain fully collateralized event contracts, which had been covered by staff no-action letters since 2017. Affected market participants will report under Parts 15 through 18 instead of certain sections of Parts 38, 39, 43, and 45. Compliance dates vary by section..

entry.title: CFTC Staff Advisory on Using Crypto Assets to Meet Financial Resources Requirements
entry.summary: CFTC Staff Issues Advisory Concerning the Use of Crypto Assets to Satisfy Financial Resources Requirements CFTC · Nov 23, 2026 · Guidance · CryptoTopic evidence: 「certain crypto assets, including bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins, may be counted toward the requirement to hold financial resources covering at least 12 months of operating costs」 The CFTC's Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued a staff advisory on how swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations may use crypto assets to meet their financial resources requirements. It says bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins may count toward holding resources that cover at least 12 months of operating costs, subject to appropriate haircuts. Because crypto assets are not "cash" or "highly liquid securities" under GAAP, they are not eligible for the separate liquidity requirement. The advisory reflects staff views only and does not create new rules or enforceable rights.

entry.title: CFTC Awards Over $11 Million to Whistleblowers
entry.summary: CFTC Grants over $11M in Whistleblower Awards CFTC · Nov 23, 2026 · EnforcementThe U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced over $11 million in awards to 14 whistleblowers whose original information led to a successful enforcement action against an extensive fraud scheme. entry.title: CFTC Charges 11 Companies and Two Indiana Executives in $550 Million Fraud Scheme
entry.summary: CFTC Charges 11 Companies and Two Indiana Executives in $550 Million Fraud Scheme CFTC · Nov 20, 2026 · EnforcementThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed a complaint in federal court in Indiana against two executives and 11 affiliated companies. It alleges they ran a Ponzi scheme that took more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants, claiming the money would fund leveraged forex trading. The complaint says little to no trading occurred, with funds misappropriated or used to pay fake profits, and solicitations continued through October 2026. The court froze assets and appointed a temporary receiver, and the CFTC seeks restitution, penalties, and a permanent injunction.
